messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary group 'wave-7' - p95 latency spike detected across runtime nodes (4.2s). Error budget bleed increasing. Auto-fallback to kernel-quant path observed on 3/6 hosts. Logs: `kernel_select: fallback->quant_kv (reason: batch_time > 200ms)`.

nate: Paging - I'm oncall. I see the alert. Initial hypothesis: batching window growth causing KV cache pressure -> kernel selector thrash -> fallback -> higher token latency.

jia: Confirmed. I pulled traces, saw micro-batches bumping to 128 tokens per microbatch unexpectedly for short inputs. Sequence length distro unchanged. Likely rollout change to adaptive_batcher in last canary.

sara: Customer ops ping: two customer tenants reported slow responses and one support ticket saying streaming timeouts. Estimated affected requests ~0.8% of hosted traffic, concentrated on wave-7 region (us-west-2).

mike: Reproduce locally with canary config: `--adaptive-batcher=true --batch-window-ms=40`. With that config we see batch windows spike under bursty traffic and KV eviction thrash. Dumps:
```
[2026-03-17T12:03:21Z] batch_window_ms=40 current_window=220ms microbatch_size=112
[2026-03-17T12:03:21Z] kv_cache_evictions=1243 kernel_fallback=quant_kv
```

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-42. Severity: Sev2. Notifying SRE rotation.

nate: Immediate actions: 1) Stop canary rollout. 2) Disable adaptive_batcher flag for wave-7. 3) If still degraded, kill-switch to rollback to previous release (v2.13.3). Who can flip flags?

jia: I can flip the feature flag in the control plane. Doing `redwoodctl feature set adaptive_batcher=false --scope=wave-7` now.

deploy-bot: Feature change acknowledged. adaptive_batcher=false applied to wave-7 (api-id: /v1/flags/abc123). Propagation ETA: ~8s.

mike: Watching metrics. p95 dropped from 4.2s -> 1.1s within one propagation window. KV eviction rate falling. Looks like flag flip helped.

sara: Customer update drafted: "We identified a canary config that increased batching aggressiveness; we've disabled it for affected hosts and are seeing latencies return to normal. No data loss; we continue monitoring." Should I send?

nate: Yes, send interim. Also escalate to PM + release owner to block re-roll until postmortem.

jia: Logging additional evidence in INC-2026-0317-42: kernel_selector trace, batching histograms, sample request IDs. I'll attach microdump and notes on why batch window grew (race in request arrival estimator).

mike: Ops note - avoid rolling the adaptive_batcher feature to other waves. I've added a release hold on release-2026.03.16 in the pipeline.

incident-bot: Oncall handoff scheduled in 45m -> paging handoff to @mike if still open.

nate: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. Mike will be primary. Key checklist for next oncall: verify no kernel_fallbacks remaining in last 30m, check kv_eviction < 50/min, confirm canary remains stable, coordinate rollback if we see reoccurrence.

mike: Acknowledged. I'll also run a constrained re-run test with `--adaptive-batcher=true --batch-window-ms=20` on staging to attempt reproducer fix before re-enabling.

jia: Postmortem notes to include: bad default for adaptive batching in new kernel selector coupling, missing guard on microbatch cap, insufficient canary throttling rules. Action items: add microbatch cap, add selector quick failover metric, tighten canary throttle limits.

sara: Support will update affected customers with incident id and ETA for RCA. Marking impact as intermittent latency (no error responses).

nate: Closing notes: kill-switch not required since flag flip mitigated. Keep INC open for RCA. If degradation returns reopen paging. Good handoff to Mike. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks team. Monitoring window 60m. I'll escalate to release owner if any spike. Filing follow-up in #eng-releases for release gating.

incident-bot: INC-2026-0317-42 status: Mitigated -> Watching. Primary: mike. Secondary: nate.

(End of thread)
